extracted.intended_audience: utilities, cable operators, telecommunications carriers (new and existing attachers), and their legal/compliance teams
extracted.subtask_description: Rules governing pole/duct/conduit attachment rates, timelines, notices, surveys, estimates, make-ready work, self-help remedies, and the one-touch make-ready process for new and existing attachers and utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation Rate Difference for GAAP opt-outs
rubrics_metrics.description: Price cap companies or rate-of-return carriers electing to opt-out of part 32 may calculate attachment rates using either part 32 or GAAP; if using GAAP within the first 12 years after opting out, they must adjust annually computed GAAP-based rates by an Implementation Rate Difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation Rate Difference = difference between attachment rates calculated under part 32 and under GAAP as of the last full year preceding the carrier's initial opting-out of part 32 USOA accounting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for unjust or unreasonable rates/terms/conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines a complained-of rate, term, or condition is not just and reasonable, it may prescribe a just and reasonable rate/term/condition and may terminate the unjust/unreasonable term, substitute the Commission-established term in the pole attachment agreement, and/or order refunds/payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds/payments normally equal the difference between amounts paid under the unjust term and amounts that would have been paid under the Commission-established term, plus interest, consistent with applicable statute of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission orders for unlawfully denied or delayed access
rubrics_metrics.description: If access to a pole, duct, conduit, or right-of-way has been unlawfully denied or delayed, the Commission may order that access be permitted within a specified timeframe and in accordance with specified rates, terms, and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation of pole attachment rates
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility that provides telecommunications or cable services must impute to its costs of providing such services (and charge any affiliate/subsidiary/associate engaged in providing such services) an amount equal to the pole attachment rate the company would be liable for under these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures internal transactions reflect the pole attachment rate liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of modification costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of modifying a facility shall be borne by all parties that obtain access as a result of the modification and by all parties that directly benefit from the modification; each shares proportionately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party with a preexisting attachment is deemed to directly benefit if, after receiving notice, it adds to or modifies its attachment. A preexisting attacher is not required to bear costs of rearranging/replacing its attachment if that rearrangement/replacement is necessitated solely by another party's additional attachment or modification. Parties attaching after completion share proportionately if modification rendered the attachment possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of unusable space costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall apportion the cost of providing unusable space on a pole so that such apportionment equals two-thirds of the costs that would be allocated to such entity under an equal apportionment among all attaching entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All attaching entities are counted for purposes of apportioning unusable space. Utilities may use rebuttable presumptive averages (non-urban: 3 attachers; urban: 5 attachers) unless they establish and justify their own presumptive averages following good faith procedures and provide methodology on request; attaching entities may challenge presumptives with data or statistically sound surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions for space factor calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: For the space-factor formulas, the space occupied by an attachment is presumed to be one foot; usable space presumed 13.5 feet; unusable space presumed 24 feet; pole height presumed 37.5 feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All these presumptions are rebuttable by either party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms used for timelines and processes: 'attachment', 'new attacher', 'existing attacher', 'Mid-Sized Order' (greater than lesser of 300 poles or 0.5% and up to lesser of 3,000 poles or 5%), and 'Large Order' (greater than lesser of 3,000 poles or 5% up to lesser of 6,000 poles or 10%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions determine which procedural deadlines and thresholds apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice for Mid-Sized and Large Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: New attachers must give written advance notice as soon as practicable, but at least 15 days before submitting a Mid-Sized Order and 60 days before submitting a Large Order; notice must include contact info, deployment areas/routes description, anticipated build-out schedule, and for Large Orders a request to meet-and-confer within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Mid-Sized Orders the advance notice requirement is only where the threshold would be exceeded by applications that are part of a single network deployment. Failure to provide required advance notice allows the utility to treat the application as initiating the advance notice period (with consequences for timeline start); if utility fails to promptly notify, the application proceeds under normal timelines without an advance notice period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet-and-confer requirement for Large Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: New attachers and utilities must meet-and-confer within 30 days after advance notice for Large Orders to negotiate processing mechanics and timing; parties shall find a mutually agreeable day/time and may meet in person, virtually, or by phone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness review and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall review a new attacher's attachment application for completeness before merit review. The utility must determine within 10 business days whether the application is complete and notify the attacher; if no response within 10 business days or a rejection without specified reasons, the application is deemed complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deemed incomplete, the utility must specify all reasons. Resubmitted applications addressing only the specified reasons are deemed complete within 5 business days; the attacher may resubmit multiple times so long as each resubmission is a bona fide attempt to correct specified deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application merit review timing and denial limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility must respond to a complete application by granting access or denying access within 45 days of receipt of a complete application (60 days for Mid-Sized Orders, 90 days for Large Orders). A utility may not deny access based on a preexisting violation not caused by the new attacher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey timing, participation, and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall complete a survey of poles covered by a complete application within 45 days (60 days for Mid-Sized Orders, 90 days for Large Orders). The utility must notify the new attacher within 15 days if it cannot meet the survey deadline. The utility must permit new attachers and existing attachers to be present for field inspections and use commercially reasonable efforts to provide at least 3 business days advance notice including date/time, location, and contractor name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new attacher conducts a survey, the utility may rely on it by notifying affected attachers and providing a copy within the survey period; a utility relying on a new-attacher survey has 15 days to make that notification instead of the applicable survey period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to cyclical pole inspection reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submitting its attachment application, a new attacher may request the utility's most recent cyclical pole inspection reports (or more recent report) for the poles in the application; the utility must provide this information within 10 business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities must retain pole inspection reports until a superseding report covering the poles is completed. After receiving inspection info, a new attacher may amend its application at any time until grant/denial; the utility may, at its option, restart response/survey deadlines or must notify the attacher of restart intent within five business days of receipt of the amended application or by the original deadline, whichever is earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate timing and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If access is not denied, the utility must present a detailed, itemized estimate (pole-by-pole where requested) of charges to perform all necessary make-ready within 14 days of completing the survey (or within 29 days for Large Orders), or within 14 days of receipt of a new-attacher survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where pole-by-pole is requested but fixed costs aren't reasonably calculable per pole, utility may present fixed costs on a per-job basis. Utility must provide documentation sufficient to determine the basis of estimated charges (projected material, labor, related costs). Utility may withdraw an outstanding estimate beginning 14 days after presentation. A new attacher may accept an estimate any time before withdrawal. After completion, if final costs differ, utility must provide a detailed, itemized final invoice (pole-by-pole where requested) with supporting documentation. Utility may not charge a new attacher to bring poles/attachments into compliance with current standards if noncompliance was due to work by a party other than the new attacher prior to the new attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-ready notice requirements and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of payment for make-ready, a utility shall immediately notify in writing all known entities with existing attachments that may be affected and, for communications space, the notice must specify where/what make-ready will be performed, set a completion date no later than 30 days after notification (or up to 75/120 for Mid-Sized/Large Orders), state existing attachers may modify attachments consistent with the make-ready before the completion date, state that if make-ready is not completed by the date the new attacher may complete it, and provide contact info for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For attachments above the communications space, similar requirements apply with a default completion date no later than 90 days (or 135/180 for Mid-Sized/Large Orders), and the utility may assert a right to 15 additional days to complete make-ready. After providing notices, the utility must provide the new attacher a copy of notices and contact info where notices were sent. The new attacher is responsible for coordinating with existing attachers to encourage completion by deadlines. Utilities must notify a new attacher as soon as practicable but no later than 15 days after receipt of payment if they cannot meet the make-ready deadline; existing attachers have parallel notice obligations. New attachers may elect self-help for make-ready the notifying party cannot do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility make-ready completion obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall complete its make-ready in the communications space by the same dates set for existing attachers or its make-ready above communications space by the same dates as existing attachers (or, if asserting its 15-day right of control, 15 days later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order-size adjustments and negotiation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The specified timelines apply to requests up to the lesser of 300 poles or 0.5% of a utility's poles in a state. For Mid-Sized Orders (greater than that up to 3,000 poles or 5%), utilities may add 15 days to survey and 45 days to make-ready periods. For Large Orders (greater than Mid-Sized up to 6,000 poles or 10%), utilities may add 45 days to survey, 15 days to estimate, and 90 days to make-ready. For orders larger than 6,000 poles or 10%, utilities shall negotiate in good faith the timing of requests. Utilities may treat multiple requests from a single new attacher filed within 30 days as one request, but shall not impose application size limits combined with frequency limits that effectively restrict attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation from time limits for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility may deviate from time limits before offering an estimate if parties have no agreement specifying rates/terms/conditions. During make-ready, a utility may deviate for good and sufficient cause that renders completion infeasible, but must immediately notify in writing the new attacher and affected existing attachers, identify affected poles, provide a detailed explanation and a new completion date, limit deviation to no longer than necessary, and resume without discrimination when returning to routine operations. A utility cannot delay completion due to a preexisting violation not caused by the new attacher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing attachers may deviate from time limits during complex make-ready for safety or service-interruption reasons; they must notify affected parties immediately, identify affected poles, explain basis, and provide a new completion date not extending beyond 60 days (105/150 for Mid-Sized/Large Orders). Deviation must be limited to necessary time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-help remedies for surveys, estimates, and make-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: If a utility fails to meet survey/estimate/make-ready deadlines, a new attacher may exercise self-help remedies: conduct the survey (using an approved contractor), prepare an estimate (using approved contractor) after the utility's deadline expires, or conduct make-ready (hire contractor) if make-ready is not complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys: new attacher must permit utility/existing attachers to be present and give 3 business days advance notice including date/time, work description, and contractor. Estimates: new attacher must wait until utility's 14-day (or 29-day for Large Orders) deadline expires, notify the utility it's exercising self-help, use an approved contractor per §1.1412, and allow the utility to review and approve the estimate at the attacher's expense (reasonable, based only on actual costs). Utility must provide written decision on self-help estimate within 14 days; acceptance subjects estimate to reconciliation; non-acceptance requires written reasons and the attacher may submit a revised estimate without restarting timeline. Make-ready: new attacher must permit presence, give at least 5 days advance notice, and notify utility/existing attachers immediately if make-ready damages equipment or causes an outage; utility/existing attacher may remediate and bill the attacher or require the attacher to fix the damage immediately at its expense. New attacher must notify affected parties within 15 days after completion and allow 90 days for inspection; affected parties have 14 days after inspection completion to notify of damage or code violations with adequate documentation; remedies include remediation billed to the new attacher or requiring the new attacher to fix issues within 14 days. Self-help is not available for pole replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-help limitation: pole replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-help remedies expressly do not permit a new attacher to perform pole replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-touch make-ready election and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: For simple make-ready, new attachers may elect the one-touch make-ready process in writing in their attachment application and must identify the simple make-ready to be performed; it's the new attacher's responsibility to ensure its contractor determines whether make-ready is simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application completeness rules (10 business days/5 business days resubmission) apply to one-touch applications. The utility must review the merits of a complete one-touch application and respond within 15 days (30/45 for Mid-Sized/Large Orders). If denied, the utility's decision must be specific and include all relevant evidence explaining how lack of capacity, safety, reliability, or engineering standards support denial. The utility may object to a contractor's designation that certain make-ready is simple; if the utility objects (specific, in writing, with evidence, made in good faith, explaining relation to safety/capacity/reliability/engineering), that make-ready is deemed complex and the objection is final and determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveys and contractors under one-touch
rubrics_metrics.description: Under one-touch, the new attacher is responsible for all required surveys and must use a contractor as specified in §1.1412(b); the new attacher must permit the utility and existing attachers to be present and provide at least 3 business days advance notice with date/time and contractor name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-ready and post-make-ready under one-touch
rubrics_metrics.description: If a one-touch application is approved and the new attacher provided 15 days prior written notice of the make-ready to affected parties, the new attacher may proceed with make-ready using a contractor for simple make-ready per §1.1412(b); prior written notice must include date/time, work description, contractor name, and provide opportunity to be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New attacher must notify affected parties immediately if make-ready causes damage or outages; utility or existing attacher may remediate and bill the new attacher or require the new attacher to fix the damage immediately. If make-ready classified as simple is later determined to be complex by either party, make-ready must halt, immediate notice given, and the affected make-ready is governed by the normal attachment process. Post-make-ready notifications mirror general process: notify within 15 days after completion, allow 90 days for inspection, affected parties have 14 days after inspection to notify of damage or code violations with documentation; remediation options as in general process.
